choices.text: Pass a Fr 12 to 14 catheter, packet unbroken and in date, about 10 to 15 cm into the nose with the suction off. Apply suction only as you withdraw, at 100 to 120 mmHg for an adult, rotating the catheter, and break the suction intermittently.
choices.note: Correct. Do not suction while you are still inserting.

choices.text: Suction on the way in at 150 mmHg so secretions are caught early.
choices.note: Suction is applied on the way out, at 100 to 120 mmHg, not on the way in.

choices.text: Insert about 25 cm and use a Fr 18 catheter as the printed size.
choices.note: The printed nasal distance is about 10 to 15 cm and the size is Fr 12 to 14.

choices.text: Keep the suction continuous with no rotation.
choices.note: The page wants rotation and intermittent suction.

scene: You are preparing the suction trolley and your protective equipment.
ask: What fluid and precautions match the page?

choices.text: Only sterile water for injection may touch the tubing. Cold boiled water is banned.
choices.note: Cold boiled water is one of the three named irrigation fluids.

choices.text: A mask is optional and gloves are optional.
choices.note: Gloves and a mask are required. Gown and face shield are the optional items.

choices.text: Irrigate with normal saline, water, or cold boiled water. Hand hygiene, gloves and a mask are required. A gown and a face shield are optional. Check the bracelet and the order, look in the mouth and nose for blockage, prop the person up, and give a verbal report. An oximeter throughout is optional, but compare the condition before and after.
choices.note: Correct. Privacy is also provided.

choices.text: No report is needed if the saturation did not change.
choices.note: The page ends with a verbal report.

scene: You are coaching a first metered-dose inhaler.
ask: Which sequence matches the ten steps?

choices.text: Hold the inhaler sideways, breathe in fast for 1 second, and do not pause between puffs.
choices.note: It is held upright, the breath is slow over 3 to 5 seconds, and you wait about 30 seconds.

choices.text: Seal the lips and also keep two finger-widths, both at the same time.
choices.note: Those are two alternative positions.

choices.text: Skip the rinse after a steroid inhaler.
choices.note: The page says to rinse after an inhaled steroid.

choices.text: Take off the cap and hold the inhaler upright. Shake it. Tip the head back and breathe out. Either hold it two finger-widths from the open mouth, or seal the lips on the mouthpiece. Press as a slow deep breath starts, over 3 to 5 seconds. Close the mouth, hold the breath for about 10 seconds, then breathe normally. Wait about 30 seconds between puffs and replace the cap. Rinse the mouth after an inhaled steroid such as QVAR, Flovent or Asmanex.
choices.note: Correct. The two mouth positions are alternatives, not two extra doses.

scene: Three inhalers are due together: a steroid, an anticholinergic and a reliever.
ask: What order and timing does the package print?

choices.text: Ventolin first, the short-acting reliever. Then Atrovent, which starts in about 15 minutes and lasts 6 to 8 hours. Then Beclofort, the steroid inhaler.
choices.note: Correct. The reliever comes before the steroid, not after it.

choices.text: Beclofort first, then Ventolin, then Atrovent.
choices.note: The printed order is Ventolin, Atrovent, then Beclofort.

choices.text: Atrovent starts in about one minute and lasts one hour.
choices.note: The page says about 15 minutes to work and 6 to 8 hours of effect.

choices.text: Any order is acceptable because the drugs do not interact in the airway.
choices.note: The page prints a sequence, with the bronchodilator first.

scene: You are following the English three-lead note, not the Chinese electrode note.
ask: Where do the English colours go?

choices.text: RA is white, LA is black and LL is red, which is the Chinese note.
choices.note: Those colours are the other note on the same page. The English note is red, yellow and green.

choices.text: RA is red, inside the rib-cage frame just under the right clavicle near the shoulder. LA is yellow, under the left clavicle at the same level. LL is green, on the left, under the pectoral muscle at the lower edge of the left rib cage.
choices.note: Correct. Do not use the white-black-red Chinese colours for this English note.

choices.text: RA is yellow and LA is red.
choices.note: In the English note red is RA and yellow is LA.

choices.text: LL is green on the right lower ribs.
choices.note: The green electrode is on the left lower rib edge.

scene: You are now following the Chinese three-lead electrode note.
ask: Which colours and sites does that note print?

choices.text: RA white, LA yellow, LL green.
choices.note: Yellow and green are the English note. The Chinese LA is black and the Chinese LL is red.

choices.text: LL is red under the right clavicle.
choices.note: The red electrode in the Chinese note is the lower-left apex lead, not RA.

choices.text: All three Chinese leads are brown chest leads.
choices.note: Brown is a 12-lead chest colour, V4, not this three-lead note.

choices.text: RA, on the right, is white at the midpoint under the right clavicle. LA, on the left, is black at the midpoint under the left clavicle. LL, lower left, is red at the midpoint of the sternal tip between the 6th and 7th ribs, the apex.
choices.note: Correct. This is a different colour set from the English red, yellow and green note.

scene: You are placing the chest leads for a 12-lead ECG.
ask: Which colours and sites match the page?

choices.text: V1 red, 4th intercostal space, right sternal edge. V2 yellow, 4th space, left sternal edge. V3 green, between V2 and V4. V4 brown, 5th space, left mid-clavicular line. V5 black, 5th space, between V4 and V6. V6 purple, 5th space, left mid-axillary line.
choices.note: Correct. V3 is not on the same rib line as V2. It sits between V2 and V4.

choices.text: V1 yellow at the 5th space, left mid-axillary line.
choices.note: That site and the purple colour belong to V6. V1 is red at the 4th right sternal edge.

choices.text: V4 green at the 4th right sternal edge.
choices.note: Green is V3, between V2 and V4. V4 is brown at the 5th left mid-clavicular line.

choices.text: V2 black and V5 red.
choices.note: V2 is yellow and V5 is black.

scene: A classmate asks why a 12-lead test does not use 12 wires on the chest.
ask: What does the page say about the electrodes?

choices.text: Twelve separate chest electrodes are required, with no gel.
choices.note: The page says ten electrodes, and the pads contain gel.

choices.text: A recording called 12-lead uses ten electrodes. Some electrodes form a pair and that pair supplies two leads. The pads stick on and have conducting gel in the centre. The other side snaps onto the cable.
choices.note: Correct. Ten electrodes is not a missing-lead error.

choices.text: The cables are tied on with micropore because the pads do not stick.
choices.note: The pads are self-sticking and snap onto the cables.

choices.text: Each electrode can supply only one lead, so ten electrodes make a 10-lead ECG.
choices.note: The page says some electrodes form a pair that provides two leads.

scene: You are laying up a bladder irrigation, not a pleural tap.
ask: Which items match the bladder list?

choices.text: A 23 gauge angiocath and an Atrium chest drain as the irrigation set.
choices.note: Those are pleural-tap items. Bladder irrigation uses the Y-set and a three-way catheter.

choices.text: Lignocaine 5 percent and a 16 gauge long angiocath.
choices.note: Those are on the abdomen-tapping list.

choices.text: An S14 dressing set, a Y irrigation set with the white end rubber removed, a three-way catheter of Fr 20 or above, Hibitane which is blue or Tisept which is yellow, a bladder syringe, xylocaine jelly, and two 2-litre measuring jars.
choices.note: Correct. Also a drip stand, Hyperfix, an irrigation bedside bag, sterile gloves and an extra blue pad.

choices.text: Leave the white end rubber on the Y-set.
choices.note: The page says to remove the white end rubber tubing.

scene: The doctor is about to tap ascites.
ask: What does the abdomen-tapping list put first, and which needle and anaesthetic does it name?

choices.text: Give intravenous albumin first if it is prescribed. Use a 16 gauge long angiocath and lignocaine 5 percent, with 70 percent alcohol and povidone. If the first attempt fails, dress the site with gauze, combined gauze and Opsite, with or without Elastoplast.
choices.note: Correct. This list is not the pleural set and it is not the bladder Y-set.

choices.text: Start with an Atrium chest bottle and 2 percent lignocaine.
choices.note: 2 percent lignocaine and the Atrium unit are on the pleural list. Abdomen tapping uses lignocaine 5 percent and a 16 gauge long angiocath.

choices.text: Albumin is given only after a failed tap.
choices.note: Albumin, if prescribed, is given before the tap.

choices.text: Use a Fr 10 Nelaton catheter as the tapping needle.
choices.note: The Nelaton is the once-only urinary catheter, not this tap.

scene: You are setting a trolley for a pleural tap.
ask: Which equipment identifies this list rather than an abdomen tap?

choices.text: A 16 gauge long angiocath and lignocaine 5 percent as the main needle and drug.
choices.note: Those are the abdomen-tap items. Pleural tapping names a 23 gauge angiocath.

choices.text: A 23 gauge angiocath, a sterile blade, suture material, an Atrium disposable chest drainage unit, thoracic trocars and cannulae in three sizes, and a keyhole dressing.
choices.note: Correct. Also a mask, a gown, a safety stand, an oximeter and a suction machine.

choices.text: A three-way Fr 20 catheter and xylocaine jelly as the drainage method.
choices.note: That is bladder irrigation.

choices.text: No drainage unit is required.
choices.note: The Atrium disposable sterile chest drainage unit is on the list.

scene: The pleural trolley is almost complete and you are checking the anaesthetic and the drain bottle.
ask: Which details match the pleural list?

choices.text: 5 percent lignocaine and no water in the chamber.
choices.note: 5 percent lignocaine is the abdomen-tap strength. The pleural list says 2 percent, and sterile water fills the chamber.

choices.text: Bare metal clamps, with the latex tubing removed.
choices.note: The blades are protected with latex tubing.

choices.text: The local anaesthetic named is 2 percent lignocaine. Sterile water is used to fill the chamber. Two pairs of clamps have their blades protected with latex tubing. A disinfectant example is 10 percent povidone iodine.

ask: Which item belongs only with the pleural trolley?

choices.text: Xylocaine jelly and a bladder syringe.
choices.note: Those are bladder-irrigation items.

choices.text: A 16 gauge long angiocath.
choices.note: That needle is on the abdomen-tap list. The pleural angiocath is 23 gauge.
